source_title: Code of Research Degree Vivas
question: How long does a research degree viva last, and what happens if it runs long?
expected_answer: The length of a viva varies, but if it lasts longer than two hours the internal examiner or Independent Chair will recommend an adjournment for a break.
follow_up_question: Who normally attends the viva?
follow_up_expected_answer: The viva normally involves only the external examiner, the internal examiner (or second external examiner) and the candidate. The Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) may appoint an Independent Chair to oversee the conduct of the oral examination. The candidate's supervisor is not normally present and may attend only in exceptional circumstances, approved individually.
follow_up_keyphrases: supervisor will not normally be present

source_title: Policy for the Appointment of Independent Chairs for Research Degree Vivas
question: In which circumstances will the Faculty Dean Postgraduate appoint an Independent Chair for a viva?
expected_answer: An Independent Chair is appointed when: the Internal Examiner has no experience in research degree examining; the Internal Examiner is new to research degree examining at Essex and has not undertaken Internal Examiner training; the viva follows a referral and resubmission of a thesis; the viva follows an appeal; there are circumstances affecting the candidate that make it desirable; the candidate is a member of staff of the University or a Partner Institution being examined as a staff candidate; or where agreed in individual cases to be necessary.
keyphrases: no experience in research degree examining
follow_up_question: Who is eligible to be nominated, and can they come from the candidate's own department?
follow_up_expected_answer: A nominee must be a permanent member of staff who has been an Internal Examiner for at least two postgraduate research examinations at Essex, or has examined two theses externally and undertaken University of Essex Independent Chair training, and must have a good understanding of the University's procedures and regulations for the award being examined. The Independent Chair chosen will be from outside the candidate's department and will have no conflict of interest with the candidate, the supervisor or the External Examiner.
follow_up_keyphrases: at least two postgraduate research examinations

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates 2025-26
question: Who must a department designate to lead each professional doctorate at Essex, and who are they responsible to?
expected_answer: Each department must designate a Professional Doctorate Director for each professional doctorate, a group of professional doctorates or equivalent, who is an experienced doctoral student supervisor. The Director is responsible to the Head of Department for the departmental arrangements for the relevant PD students, and liaises with and reports as necessary to the Dean.
follow_up_question: Which Dean do professional doctorate decisions normally get referred to?
follow_up_expected_answer: In practice most decisions are referred to the Faculty Dean Postgraduate through the Postgraduate Research Education Team. 'Dean' refers to the Executive Dean (or their deputy) or the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy).

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: For Tavistock and Portman professional doctorates, who is designated to lead each programme and who are they responsible to?
expected_answer: The Trust designates a Course Lead for each Professional Doctorate, a group of professional doctorates or equivalent, who is an experienced doctoral student supervisor. The Course Lead is responsible to the Portfolio Manager for the Trust arrangements for the relevant PD students.
follow_up_question: Which Dean do decisions get referred to for these programmes?
follow_up_expected_answer: For Tavistock and Portman professional doctorates, 'Dean' refers to the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy), and most decisions are referred to the Dean of Partnerships through the Postgraduate Research Education Team.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: Can a viva be waived for a professional doctorate, and who decides?
expected_answer: Permission to waive a viva on first submission will only be granted by the Dean in exceptional circumstances. The Postgraduate Research Education Team would then notify the student of the examiners' wish not to hold a viva and the reasons for it, and the student would be told they have the right to have a viva if they wish.
follow_up_question: What if the thesis has been referred?
follow_up_expected_answer: Where a thesis has been referred, the rules for waiving the viva on a referred thesis apply as set out in the Code of Practice, separately from the first-submission case.

source_title: PGT Modular Rules of Assessment 2025-26
question: A student has failed a core taught module with a mark of 45. Can that failure be condoned?
expected_answer: No. Condonement applies only to non-core modules - failure with a mark of 40 or more may be condoned for up to 20 credits in non-core modules. All taught core modules must be passed, so a failed core module cannot be condoned regardless of the mark.
follow_up_question: How many credits can be condoned in total?
follow_up_expected_answer: Failure with a mark of 40 or more may be condoned for up to 20 credits in non-core modules, provided the other progression requirements are met.

source_title: Code of Research Degree Vivas
question: Both examiners have read the thesis and think the candidate is likely to be referred. They would rather not hold a viva. Can it be waived?
expected_answer: No. Vivas will not be waived where one or more examiners has deemed from reading the thesis that the candidate seems likely to fail, to only be eligible for a lower award, or to be referred.
follow_up_question: What happens to a candidate who will not engage with viva arrangements at all?
follow_up_expected_answer: A candidate who does not engage with the arrangements to the extent that it has not been possible to arrange a viva shall be deemed to have withdrawn permanently from the University and from their research degree, unless it has been agreed that the viva can be waived.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: We would like a visiting academic to supervise one of our PGR students. Is that permitted?
expected_answer: Not as a supervisor in the normal sense - visiting staff cannot be appointed as a supervisor of a PGR student unless they are formally appointed via the associate supervisor route.
follow_up_question: Does the same restriction apply on professional doctorates?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. The Code of Practice for Professional Doctorates carries the same restriction: visiting staff cannot be appointed as a supervisor of a PGR student unless formally appointed via the associate supervisor route.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates 2025-26
question: Can a professional doctorate student's standard period of study be shortened, and whose approval is needed?
expected_answer: Yes, but only in exceptional circumstances and with the Deans' approval. The standard period of study may be reduced in exceptional circumstances with the Deans' approval.
keyphrases: standard period of study may be reduced
follow_up_question: What is expected of a student entering a completion period?
follow_up_expected_answer: A student entering a completion period does so on the understanding that their full thesis will be ready for submission by the end of that completion period.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: A referred thesis has come back and the examiners recommend a pass. Do we still need to hold a second viva?
expected_answer: Not necessarily. Where the recommendation on the referred thesis is a pass, a request by the examiners to waive the viva will normally be granted. Where the recommendation is not a pass, a waiver will only be granted in exceptional circumstances.
follow_up_question: And on first submission?
follow_up_expected_answer: On first submission, permission to waive a viva will only be granted by the Dean in exceptional circumstances. The Postgraduate Research Education Team would notify the student of the examiners' wish not to hold a viva and the reasons, and the student would be told they have the right to have a viva if they wish.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: A Supervisory Panel wants to discontinue a student. Can the Panel make that decision itself?
expected_answer: No. A decision or recommendation for discontinuation, downgrading or upgrading, to confirm PhD status or change to MPhil, to permit entry into completion, or to extend the standard period can only be made by the RSPB. The Supervisory Panel can only recommend.
follow_up_question: Are there any restrictions on who sits on the RSPB for that decision?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. Where the RSPB is considering a recommendation of discontinuation or downgrading, or a change of status to MPhil at confirmation, the RSPB membership must include at least two members who were not on the student's last Supervisory Panel. Smaller departments may co-opt a supervisor from another department in a cognate discipline to satisfy this.
follow_up_keyphrases: at least two members who were not

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates 2025-26
question: Can the student's main supervisor chair their Supervisory Panel?
expected_answer: No. The chair must not be a partner or close relative of the supervisor (main, joint or secondary), and must not have a professional or personal relationship with the student that might give rise to a conflict of interest.
follow_up_question: What happens if a professional practice supervisor has to step down partway through?
follow_up_expected_answer: Where a professional practice supervisor cannot continue supervision for whatever reason, the department must ensure that a replacement supervisor is appointed.

source_title: Code of Research Degree Vivas
question: A supervisor has asked to sit in on their student's viva. Is that allowed, and who decides?
expected_answer: Not normally. The candidate's supervisor will not normally be present at the viva and can only be present in exceptional circumstances, approved on an individual basis by the Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) and with the agreement of the examiners. It is good practice for the supervisor to be invited to attend at the end of the viva when the examiners communicate their recommendation.
follow_up_question: Can they be there when the outcome is given?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes - it is good practice for the supervisor to be invited to attend at the end of the viva when the examiners communicate their recommendation to the candidate.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: Our PGR student is sponsored under a Student visa. Can their supervision meetings be held over Zoom?
expected_answer: Only to a limited extent. For students with immigration sponsorship the majority of contact should be face-to-face; in exceptional circumstances the University may agree that contact can be via video link. Virtual meetings must not breach progress monitoring requirements for students subject to immigration control.
keyphrases: majority of contact should be face-to-face
follow_up_question: Is it different for Distance Learning students?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. There is no general requirement for Distance Learning students to attend face-to-face Supervisory Panels and they may have all Supervisory Panels held via Zoom if deemed more appropriate. If a department wishes to require face-to-face panels or other on-campus activity for a Distance Learning student, that must be specified when the details of the arrangement are set.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: If a student is granted an extension, does that affect how much completion time they have left?
expected_answer: Yes. In such instances the subsequent number of completion periods available to the student will be reduced by one term, unless exceptional circumstances make that reduction inappropriate. Students must be offered an opportunity to discuss this with the RSPB before the final recommendation is forwarded to the Dean for approval.
follow_up_question: Can an extension of more than one term ever be granted?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes - in exceptional circumstances an extension of more than one term may be granted.

source_title: PGT Modular Rules of Assessment 2025-26
question: A student resubmits an assessment for a module they had already passed overall. Can their module mark go up?
expected_answer: No. If the pre-resubmission module aggregate was above the pass mark, the resubmission cannot improve the module aggregate mark - the module aggregate is capped at the pre-resubmission aggregate.
follow_up_question: And if they had failed the module overall?
follow_up_expected_answer: If the pre-resubmission module aggregate was below the pass mark, the resubmission can improve the module aggregate mark up to the pass mark only.

source_title: PGT Programme Credit Framework 2025-26
question: Does an exit award have to carry the same title as the main programme?
expected_answer: Normally yes - the title of the exit award will be the same as for the main programme, unless a different title has been approved in order to meet Professional, Statutory or Regulatory Body requirements.
follow_up_question: Which awards does the credit framework actually cover?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Postgraduate Taught Programme Credit Framework covers Masters degrees, PG Diplomas, PG Certificates, and Integrated Masters degrees (Final Stage only).

source_title: Policy for the Appointment of Independent Chairs for Research Degree Vivas
question: Our department has 160 PGR students. How many Independent Chair nominations do we have to put forward?
expected_answer: Four. Departments with 150 or more PGR students must put forward 4 nominations (1-99 require 2, 100-149 require 3).
follow_up_question: Do departments without any PGR students have to nominate anyone?
follow_up_expected_answer: No - but they may if they wish. All departments are able to nominate Independent Chairs to be approved by the Faculty Education Committee, including those without PGR students if they wish.

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: For a Tavistock professional doctorate, who can decide to permit a student to enter their completion period?
expected_answer: Only the RSPB. A decision or recommendation for discontinuation or downgrading, to permit entry into completion, or to extend the standard period can only be made by the RSPB.
keyphrases: can only be made by the RSPB
follow_up_question: Who does the Course Lead report to for these programmes?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Course Lead is responsible to the Portfolio Manager for the Trust arrangements for the relevant PD students, and liaises with and reports as necessary to the Dean - which for these programmes is the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy).
follow_up_keyphrases: Portfolio Manager for the Trust arrangements

source_title: Code of Research Degree Vivas
question: A candidate keeps failing to respond about viva arrangements and we cannot get one scheduled. What is the position?
expected_answer: A candidate who does not engage in viva arrangements to the extent that it has not been possible to arrange a viva shall be deemed to have withdrawn permanently from the University and from their research degree, unless it has been agreed that the viva can be waived.
follow_up_question: What if they cannot engage because of exceptional circumstances?
follow_up_expected_answer: The Code provides for waiving the viva where there are exceptional circumstances which prevent a candidate from engaging in the viva process, so the withdrawal position would not apply in that case.

expected_answer: The policies do not set out a process for switching between full-time and part-time PhD registration. The correct response is to say that this is not covered by the available documents, rather than describing supervisory panel or completion-period arrangements, which address different matters.
follow_up_question: Is there anything on the paperwork or approvals involved?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. The documents do not describe the paperwork or approvals for a change of study mode, and the assistant should say so rather than substituting related but different provisions.

question: How much is the PGR tuition fee for a part-time professional doctorate this year?
expected_answer: The policy and rules-of-assessment documents do not contain fee amounts. The correct response is to say that fee levels are not covered by these documents rather than quoting a figure.
follow_up_question: What about the fee for a writing-up year?
follow_up_expected_answer: Also not covered. The documents do not state fee amounts for any year of study, and the assistant should say so.

question: Which members of staff are currently on the approved pool of Independent Chairs?
expected_answer: The policy describes how Independent Chairs are nominated and approved but does not list the individuals on the pool. The correct response is to say the names are not available in these documents, while optionally noting that Faculty Education Committees approve the list annually.
follow_up_question: Can you tell me how many there are in each department?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. The policy states how many nominations each department must put forward based on PGR student numbers, but does not record actual current numbers or names per department.
